THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE  209

Acceptance of Building:
    On behalf of founders, Mrs. Annie Halsell Woodward, Durant, Oklahoma.
    On behalf of sponsors, Mr. J. Wesley Moulton, Superintendent of School, Savoy.
Song, "Savoy College Days," Lena Pace Hodges, Author, Hollywood, California.
Adjournment.


SAVOY COLLEGE DAYS

Tune, "Auld Lang Syne"

Dedicated to former Teachers and Students of Savoy College.

                    I.
            Should friends and schoolmates be forgot
            In days that used to be?
            Brave lads and lassies kind were we,
                In dear old College days.

                    II.
            Today we pay a tribute true,
            We give a toast for you—
            Old students—friends of days gone by,
                And our dear President, too.

                    III.
            And now we sing our praise of you—
            Our guide through College years.
            You made our problems easy, too,
            As we smiled through our tears.
            We sing All Hail—All Hail to you—
                Our Alma Mater Dear.
                    —Lena Pace Hodges, Hollywood, California.

    After the last course was served, a waiting crowd of perhaps five hundred more people was admitted to the gymnasium seats to witness and hear the program which followed, and still others remained on open-air seats erected in front of the building and heard the program through loudspeaker extensions.

    Facing this combined crowd of well over seven hundred people, Mr. Gus W. Thomasson proved a most capable and spirited toastmaster. After the invocation by Judge Oliver C. Mulkey, of Commerce, Texas, Mr. Thomasson delivered the keynote address entitled "After Fifty Years."
